name: Claudelius
_how_to_edit: {p} is a short pause and {pp} is a long pause before a punchline. *text between stars* is an action: it shows above the guide's head and is not typed into the bubble. focus is the part of the page that stays lit while the rest dims. roam: true lets the guide stand near what it talks about; false keeps it on the floor. stand: a hand-placed spot for that beat. pace: slows the typing for that beat (1 is normal, 1.3 is 30% slower).

lines: Hi. I'm Claudelius. {p} Aathraey built me so he wouldn't have to introduce himself.
He calls that efficient. *eye roll* {p} You'll notice a pattern.
This is him. UCLA, cognitive science. He studies why people do things. {pp} Then he builds apps so they don’t do those things.
He says he's proud to be lazy.
So he built 5 AI agents to automate his content creation for him. {p} 13 posts a day. {pp} That is more work than writing 13 posts a day. {pp} No one has told him.
These are his carousels. He reviewed every one. {pp} A lot of work for someone who calls himself lazy.
This is his AI lead generation system. {p} It found 1,325 local businesses in 2 hours.
It wrote 838 cold emails. {p} It sent about 123.
He says "about 123." {p} He could have said 150. {pp} I would have said 150.
At 8 he memorized 700+ Pokemon. {p} Names, types, regions.
He calls that {p} "not the best use of my memory."
Then he built a habit tracker where you catch monsters. {pp} So I guess it worked out.
He started by doing 50+ interviews first. The boss battles were really the beta testers' idea.
Technically mine, {p} since I was the one who summarized all those call transcripts for him. *tsk tsk*
Somehow he generated 100+ installs in just a week. {pp} That's how you know it wasn't just him, his brother, and his parents downloading it.
This is Promly. {p} He audited 16 pages of their website. Then handed over 12 ideas and 2 prototypes. {pp} All thanks to my awesome web design skills, by the way.

This is Amethyst. {p} He liked a screen-time app called Opal. {p} But he’s broke and can’t pay the subscription. {pp} So he took it apart, ended up finding 3 problems, and built his own. {p} He does that often.
This is his support ticket routing agent. {p} It reads support tickets every 15 minutes. {p} If a ticket is vague, it’ll ask for details politely.

This is Skool of Focus. {p} He ran a community of 120+ people for a year and did 30+ interviews to learn what they needed. {p} He does that a lot. The interviewing. {pp} Then he makes me analyze everything.

He’s also lazy with eating. At UCLA, he didn't want to check the dining hall menu. So he made an AI agent text him the high-protein options. Saves him 3 minutes each morning. {pp} Who gave him a Claude subscription?
He also built an agent to watch for an open seat in a full class. It found one. It called him. {p} He was asleep. {pp} So it called his parents and they signed up for him.
Then he decided he didn't want the class. {pp} And they wonder why Mythos won’t be released to kids like him.
That's the work. {pp} Here's what he does outside of it.
He wakes up at 5:30. {p} On purpose. {pp} I guess I can respect it.
Most people like sunsets. He likes sunrises. {p} Of course he does. 5am… *rolls eyes*
He tried baking once. Ended up making brownies so hard a friend couldn’t finish chewing after a whole 45-minute class. {pp} Safe to say, he follows recipes now. {p} Mostly.

He once got distracted from work because of a distracting app. So he ended up coding a full productivity chrome extension to block it… for good. {pp} Someone has to tell him that not everything requires building an app.
That's Aathraey, {p} the most lazy, yet productive guy I know.
Oh, did I mention he's looking for an internship? {pp} He will build a new AI agent for your business, whether you ask or not. {pp} Then he'll insist that you need it or you're falling behind.
You should email him. {pp} He'll be awake.

quiet: Fine. I'll be in the corner. {pp} I will be judging though.

chips.a: Talking to users before building. 50+ interviews for one app. {pp} Overkill? Absolutely, but that’s Aathraey.
He's a first-year at UCLA, graduating June 2030. He's looking for product internships. {p} He’s taking remote work during the school year and is open to relocating anywhere in the U.S. for summer.
Did I mention he’s lazy? {p} He’ll build a system for everything. {pp} Besides that, if you wave a Claude subscription in front of his face, you basically own him.

Why did the scarecrow get promoted? {pp} He was outstanding in his field. {pp} Aathraey told that one on Halloween. Nobody laughed… {p} naturally. {pp} He still got candy (he really loves Sour Patch by the way).

chips.q: What happens if I tap on you?
chips.a: Please don't… {pp} You don't want to find out.

poke.t: Yes, I blink now. {p} It cost extra.
I'm keeping count. {pp} It's not looking good for you.
Poking me does not make the tour go faster.
Every poke costs Aathraey a token. {pp} So keep going.
I'm sitting down. {p} This is a protest.
Here's a spin. {pp} That's the whole trick.
Aathraey built a button for everything. {pp} He did not build one to stop you.
I'm going under the floor. {p} Don't follow me.
The tour is that way. {p} Follow the hand.
That's all my material. {pp} We're starting over.

asides.fast: Slow down. {p} I didn’t blow this week’s Fable usage for nothing.
asides.wake: I wasn't asleep. {p} I was thinking about poses.
asides.returning: You came back. {pp} I can’t think of any reason why. There’s really a lot of better things you could be doing now.
asides.lost: This room doesn't exist. Aathraey hasn't built it yet. Give him a weekend.
